doctrine.canonicalOwnership: Civic Timeline is a temporal projection. Domain records remain canonical in their existing owner.
doctrine.projectionRule: Project only a date/time that means an occurrence, deadline, effective change, sourced target, or publication/release. Never treat review/check/as-of metadata or an observation period as a public civic occurrence.
doctrine.sourceChangeRule: A source-change signal is a review candidate, not a public timeline item.
doctrine.duplicateRule: When a City Monitor record is already linked to a canonical domain record, the timeline should project the domain owner and use City Monitor as provenance/evidence rather than publish two timeline identities.

dateSemantics.meaning: A meeting, session, hearing, assembly, closure or other sourced occurrence date/time.
A sourced citizen, filing, procurement, election or service deadline.
A sourced effective/start/end date for a rule, closure, service change or other civic state.
The date a record, report, dataset, audit or other civic information was actually published/released.
A source-backed target date may project when precision is sufficient and the canonical owner clearly distinguishes target from achieved outcome.
The period a statistic or fiscal value describes. It is not the date the information was published.
A broad period label such as 2025, Q2 2025 or Current. It cannot be used as a public timeline occurrence without a more precise date.
checkedOn, reviewedOn, lastVerified, reconciledOn and similar maintenance metadata.
A date proving a record was current as of a review point; not itself a civic occurrence unless an underlying effective change date is sourced.

strengths: A common dated record model already spans council sessions, legislation, procurement, projects, publications, consultations and notices.
City Monitor already runs a daily source-monitor workflow.
constraints: The record date is type-dependent and must be mapped to a precise semantic before projection.
Several monitored sources are reachability-only; a changed/reachable page does not identify a public occurrence.
When a linked canonical domain record exists, City Monitor must not become a duplicate timeline identity.

geography: relationships to barangay/place/service/project when explicitly modeled
strengths: Lifecycle already distinguishes filing, readings, council approval, mayoral action, publication, effectivity, implementation, amendment and repeal.
Session evidence can point to a City Monitor record.
constraints: Only lifecycle/session rows with an explicit date may project.
Incomplete lifecycle coverage must remain visible as a coverage gap.

geography: citywide unless a source explicitly scopes the session/hearing
strengths: Session date and session type are already structured.
constraints: Current official video listing is not a complete legislative calendar.
Stable item-specific source URLs are still missing for some sessions.
Transcript processing timestamps are maintenance metadata, not civic occurrences.

existingTemporalFields: Public Record period labels for election rules/registration
strengths: Historical election dates are exact and canonical.
constraints: Future voter-registration deadlines and election milestones are not yet a canonical structured dataset.
PublicRecord.period cannot be converted into a deadline without item-level official dates.
doNotProject: election result publication assumptions without a sourced release date

strengths: Selected procurement rows already have exact bid dates; some project/commitment entries carry target dates and later public evidence.
constraints: Many targetDate values are broad strings such as quarters, not exact dates.
Contract, notice-to-proceed, implementation and completion linkage remains incomplete for many procurements.
period and lastVerified are not occurrence dates.

geography: citywide by default; topic/domain relationships may provide narrower scope later
strengths: Each report already has a stable slug, canonical URL and date field.
constraints: Before projecting automatically, FeaturedReportV2.date must be formally defined as the BetterMakati report publication/release date rather than a general review date.
Source publishedOrPeriod describes sources, not necessarily the report release.

strengths: Indicators already preserve period, geography, source IDs and publication/provisional/revised observation status.
constraints: Observation period/asOf means when the statistic applies, not when the dataset was released.
Source checkedAt is maintenance metadata.
A release/catalogued date must be captured separately before Statistics can project 'newly published' items.

strengths: Records already have stable IDs, publishers, categories, source class, canonical contexts and URLs.
constraints: period is descriptive metadata, not a publication or first-seen timestamp.
Need cataloguedAt/firstSeenAt or a source-backed publishedAt before a record can appear in Recently Published.

existingTemporalFields: No canonical deadline/effective-date field in ServiceDirectoryItem
geography: citywide; barangay for barangay-owned services where explicitly scoped
strengths: Stable service IDs provide excellent canonical targets for future deadlines and changes.
constraints: Current service directory is largely durable guidance; scheduled availability mentioned in prose is not a structured date.
Deadlines/temporary service changes require official item-level notices.
doNotProject: generic annual-renewal language without a sourced date
source document year as a service deadline

strengths: All 23 barangays have stable canonical slugs and dedicated pages.
constraints: Assemblies, local advisories and dated notices are not structured today.
Official social/page coverage is uneven and may require manual-review adapters.
doNotProject: official term label as an occurrence
service availability prose without a date

strengths: Transport services, routes, stations, places and selected geometries already have canonical identities.
constraints: Current statusAsOf/reviewedOn/reconciledOn are verification dates, not service-change effective dates.
Road closures and temporary disruptions need item-level official advisory records.

cityMonitorSourceStreams.note: Reachability does not identify a new measure or its lifecycle date.
Only source-backed publication dates with durable civic relevance should appear; do not turn the calendar into a speech feed.
Session identity/date can project after stable item evidence is preserved.
Social broadcasts are discovery/evidence, not automatic timeline items.
Only civic/service/public-information occurrences should be promoted; generic entertainment stays excluded.
A changed news page requires item-level extraction and canonical routing.
Exact item and milestone date are required.
A page hash change is not an exact Makati procurement match.
Need item-level publication identity and release date.

additionalSourceGaps.need: Structured current/future COMELEC milestones relevant to Makati, including registration and election deadlines.
Item-level assembly, hearing, service and advisory notices from official barangay/city channels.
Official road closure, route change and temporary transport advisory items with effective windows.
Official dataset release/publication timestamps distinct from observation periods and BetterMakati check dates.
Catalogued/first-seen timestamp and source publication date when available.
Official item-level dates for renewals, application windows and temporary service changes.
